description: Roboto Studio dependency policy. Repos extend this LAST so it wins over vendor presets: extends: [..., "local>robotostudio/.github"].

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Dependabot owns CVEs. Off here so both bots don't file for the same one.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly lockfile refresh, which is what stops PRs rotting into conflicts. Not auto-merged: Renovate delegates it to the package manager, so minimumReleaseAge cannot apply and it could pull a package published minutes ago.

packageRules.description: Everything non-major in one PR, merged by the bot on green CI. minimumReleaseAge is re-asserted here because sanity-io's min-age-exceptions preset zeroes it for @types/*, @next/*, pnpm and others that ride this group. `bump` and `lockfileUpdate` are listed because rangeStrategy:bump produces them.
Pre-1.0 packages: semver gives no compatibility guarantee below 1.0, so a minor bump can break. Own group, because one non-automerge member would disable automerge for the whole grouped PR.
CI workflow definitions move together, separately from npm. Non-major only; majors fall through to the majors rule.
Anything defining the contract with a consumer or the runtime. Breaking these breaks downstream, so a person reads the changelog.
Majors raise their own PR for review. Never auto-merged.
Framework core moves in lockstep and gets human eyes. minimumReleaseAge is re-asserted because sanity-io's min-age-exceptions preset zeroes it for these exact packages.

The surfaces a type check cannot vouch for: the Studio itself, the data/preview wiring, and Presentation. Everything else Sanity ships is a library that fails compilation when it breaks, so it rides the auto-merged group - which is also sanity-io's own posture. minimumReleaseAge is re-asserted because their min-age-exceptions preset zeroes it here.
Re-assert the org soak LAST so it survives any ecosystem preset that zeroes minimumReleaseAge for its own packages.
